behavior_summary: On 2022-01-23 at 12:54:24 and 12:54:38 UTC, two failed Dovecot/PAM authentications for user shane.watson were logged on the mail host davey_mail, both from internal address 192.168.231.56. The same address produced the same failure pattern for shane.watson (and once for andrea.moss) on 2022-01-21 and 2022-01-22, at a low rate of a few attempts per day, with no successful login, no VPN session record, and no other auth activity from that address. The rest of the host's auth log is routine root cron session open/close pairs at regular intervals before and after the window, so the flagged minute stands out only because it contains the sporadic failed logins rather than any change in host behavior.

On 2022-01-23 the VPN server logged repeated TLS renegotiation failures for user jhall from 192.168.230.165:59814: a soft reset at 14:53:54 was followed by three rounds of 'TLS key negotiation failed to occur within 60 seconds' and 'TLS handshake failed' at 14:54:54, 14:56:09 and 14:57:24, with the session moved to TM_LAME_DUCK and finally torn down by an inactivity ping-restart at 14:57:54. The same user and source address had an established session earlier in the day (soft resets at 13:05:38 and 13:59:46) and reconnected normally at 16:24:32 on a new port (59384), receiving a new virtual IP 10.9.0.6 and a standard PUSH_REPLY. The pattern is consistent with a client-side network/connectivity interruption during renegotiation rather than credential misuse; no other users or hosts appear in the window and overall VPN volume for the day is in line with surrounding days.

During the incident window, user jhall connected over SSH with a public key from 172.19.131.174 to intranet_server (session 111, ending 16:23:04) and then to mail (session 264, 16:24:36-16:25:08), with audit records showing auid 1002 on intranet_server and auid 1003 on mail. The same source address had been browsing the intranet WordPress site and the mail webmail/calendar application in the preceding hour, and it appears throughout the logs as a routine internal client. Separately, mail logged a failed dovecot authentication for alyssa.hayes from 172.19.130.4 at 15:56:45, while 172.19.130.4 otherwise shows thousands of successful dovecot authentications (e.g. traci.stevenson at 16:20:50). Both hosts also show routine root cron sessions and phpsessionclean service restarts around 16:09.

Between 03:56 and 04:00 UTC on 2022-01-24, activity from 172.19.131.174 and from 192.168.230.122 (the VPN address of user jhall, connected since 03:01) hit many internal hosts at once. The traffic included Nmap Scripting Engine probes (/, /sdk, /nmaplowercheck..., /HNAP1) against webserver and cloud_share, WPScan requests and WordPress path probes (/xmlrpc.php, /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, /admin.php, /.hta) against intranet_server, and short SSH connections that ended without an identification string on inet-dns, inet-firewall, intranet_server, morris_mail, davey_mail, internal_share, mail, cloud_share, webserver and the VPN host. The same window also contains DNS lookups from 192.168.230.4 for long random subdomains under kennedy-mendoza.info that resolve to 195.128.194.168, and the VPN session for jhall continued with a TLS soft reset at 03:59:37. Most web probes were refused with 403 or returned 404, and the SSH events are connection attempts without a completed login.

The flagged window on the vpn host contains a single sshd message that no identification string was received from 10.9.0.10, which is the VPN pool address assigned to user jhall's OpenVPN session from 192.168.230.122. In the same minutes that address performed Nmap-style HTTP probing of the webserver (HNAP1, /sdk, nmaplowercheck, all 403) and generated long random-subdomain DNS lookups for payroll_2019.xlsx.email-19.kennedy-mendoza.info resolving to 195.128.194.168. The vpn host otherwise shows routine OpenVPN certificate verification and reconnects for jhall and periodic root cron PAM sessions, so the auth line itself is a minor connection artifact rather than a login.

At 04:37:25 the web server intranet_server received a request from 172.19.131.174 (python-requests) for a PHP file in the WordPress uploads directory, with a base64-encoded wp_meta parameter that decodes to a bash reverse-shell command targeting 192.168.230.122:47124; the request returned 200 with a large response. Seconds later the web server user www-data (uid 33) used su to open a session as jhall on pts/1, and jhall then ran sudo to list privileges and execute 'cat /etc/shadow' as root from the uploads directory. Earlier, the same source IP had performed Nmap-style probing of the intranet server (nmaplowercheck, /sdk, /HNAP1) around 03:57, and the host had prior WPScan and WordPress enumeration activity. In parallel, inet-firewall and inet-dns logged repeated long random-subdomain DNS queries for payroll_2019.xlsx.email-19.kennedy-mendoza.info resolving to 195.128.194.168 from internal hosts 10.143.0.103 and 192.168.230.4, which is separate DNS-tunnel-like traffic.

On the mail server, the internal address 172.19.130.4 made repeated Dovecot/PAM authentications for many different accounts (toby.white, alyssa.hayes, traci.stevenson, rebecca.blake and others) throughout the day, which is the normal pattern for this host. In the flagged window, toby.white failed authentication twice (16:22:54 and 16:23:06) and then succeeded at 16:23:23, after which several more successful authentications for the same account followed within a second. The two failures are the only unusual element; the volume of logins in that hour (178 audit events, 2 failures) matches the host's ordinary daytime activity, and the same source produced occasional single failures on earlier days.
